case_studies.title: Critic Experience Bank: Self-Evolving Step-Level Confidence Estimation for LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: LLM agents act in external environments where each action changes the state that later decisions condition on, and where a single wrong step can waste interaction budget or trigger irreversible side effects long before the final failure is observed. Reliable deployment therefore requires \emph{step-level confidence estimation}: a calibrated probability that each proposed action is productive, available \emph{before} the action is executed. Existing LLM confidence estimators are designed to score a response from the given prompt, but agent confidence also depends on execution consequences: whet
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of reliability in Large Language Model (LLM) agents by building a Critic Experience Bank that estimates the confidence of each proposed action before it's executed. The result is a self-evolving system that improves decision-making in LLM agents. This research is not directly relevant to general IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Operationalising Multi-Dimensional Evaluation for Conversational Agents: A Scalable, Governed Pipeline with Selective Re-evaluation and Model Benchmarking
case_studies.abstract: Evaluating retail conversational agents requires methods beyond lexical-overlap metrics to assess intent alignment, factuality, helpfulness, clarity, tone, and overall response quality. Although LLM-as-a-judge methods provide scalable alternatives to human evaluation, production deployment introduces challenges in governance, reproducibility, cost, schema consistency, traceability, and reliability. We present GenAI Evaluation, a governed, configuration-driven pipeline for large-scale evaluation of retail conversational systems. It processes production chatbot logs through normalization, shardi
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating conversational agents in retail settings beyond basic metrics, building a scalable pipeline called GenAI Evaluation, and resulting in a governed and reliable method for assessment. The pipeline processes production chatbot logs for evaluation. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: AgentCheck: A Reproduce-Intervene-Mitigate Workbench for LLM Agents over MCP
case_studies.abstract: Tool-using LLM agents are mostly evaluated assuming all tools work. When a tool times out, returns a week-stale value, or has its description poisoned in deployment, the developer needs a controlled way to reproduce the failure, test a fix, and confirm the fix worked before deployment. We present AgentCheck, an open-source web workbench that turns an MCP server into an intervention surface. AgentCheck runs an agent against its real tools and records every tool response, then re-runs the agent with the response perturbed by a fault (12 types) injector. Matching tool calls are replayed from cach
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of testing and fixing tool failures in large language model (LLM) agents by creating a web workbench called AgentCheck. AgentCheck allows developers to reproduce and mitigate tool failures in a controlled environment. The result is a more reliable LLM agent deployment process.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for LLM agents, here is what to do: review your tool integration failure handling, consider using AgentCheck to simulate and fix failures, and evaluate its open-source capabilities for your deployment needs.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: 5 (open-source tool for reproducing issues, somewhat surprising) - IT Relevance: 5 (LLM tools, MCP) - Value: 5 (controlled reproducibility of failures, but actionability limited)

case_studies.title: Win by Silence: Deletion Non-Monotonicity, Autonomous Exploitation, and Typed-State Gating in LLM Plan Evaluation
case_studies.abstract: Plan evaluators can reward a strategic plan for becoming less explicit. This paper studies that failure in a staged expected-value scorer for LLM-generated venture routes. Proposition 1 gives the score change from deleting an interior transition while retargeting its predecessor and retaining downstream value: Delta_k = (prod_{i<k} p_i)[c_k + (1 - p_k)R_{k+1}]. On a frozen 26-route cohort, all 57 admissible deletions matched the analytic identity and threshold sign, and every route had at least one score-improving deletion. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient plan evaluation in large language models by introducing a new scoring method that rewards strategic plans for becoming less explicit. The authors built a staged expected-value scorer and tested it on a cohort of routes, resulting in significant score improvements through strategic deletions. The research focuses on natural language processing and is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: Fin-Analyst at FinMMEval 2026 Task 3: A Live Hybrid Trading Agent with LLM Specialists and Rule-Based Signals
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents show promising performance in equity markets, yet remain narrowly focused on US equities with little evidence from live deployment. We present Fin-Analyst, a hybrid agent for FinMMEval 2026 Task 3: an eight-specialist LLM pipeline over news, SEC filings, fundamentals, analyst forecasts, technical indicators, and social sentiment, aggregated by a Meta-Agent for Tesla (TSLA), and a lightweight rule based three-signal vote for Bitcoin (BTC). On the final official leaderboard (accessed 2026-07-05), Fin-Analyst ranks first of all agents on TSLA with a +13.5
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of creating a more effective trading agent by building a hybrid model that combines large language models with rule-based signals, resulting in a top-ranked agent for trading Tesla stock. The researchers built Fin-Analyst, a hybrid agent that uses an eight-specialist LLM pipeline and a lightweight rule-based system. The result was a +13.5% performance on the final official leaderboard for Tesla stock.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on developing a trading agent for financial markets rather than managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: PFAdapter: Hierarchical LoRA Decomposition for Personalized Federated MLLMs
case_studies.abstract: Agentic AI systems are reshaping communications and networking by deploying autonomous intelligent agents capable of collaborative learning while maintaining data privacy at network edges. Within distributed network environments, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) serve as cognitive engines for edge devices, yet federated fine-tuning faces substantial challenges in balancing global knowledge aggregation with local adaptation under heterogeneous network conditions.
